correctness.rationale: Diagonal phase covariance of zero-temperature amplitude damping reduces arbitrary U to a real rotation with s²=t=|<1|U|0>|². Four composed Kraus matrices give the normalized 4x4 Choi partial-transpose determinant 16 det J^Gamma=a²[(1-a)²(1-b)²t⁴-b²]. For two qubits the partial transpose of a positive Choi state has at most one strictly negative eigenvalue, by product-vector intersection of every 2D complex subspace. Thus determinant sign determines PPT away from zero; boundary PPT follows by lowering b to a strictly PPT region and continuity. Peres–Horodecki gives entanglement breaking iff PPT. Hence threshold (1-a)(1-b)t²>=b. Optimizing t<=1 gives b<=(1-a)/(2-a), equal a=b gives q<=(3-√5)/2. An independent 250-case random unitary-parameter numeric Choi eigenvalue/determinant comparison corroborated all threshold regions; source verify.py was inspected but not blindly executed. The determinant identity, not finite samples, is the proof.
